records.text: Corby Hall is the inventor, founder, and sole owner of FoldAR, which produces compact rifles deployable from a standard backpack.
records.speaker: Corby Hall

appearances.snippet: Well, I own a company called FoldAR. I've got the patent on the most compact AR-15 in the world, and our mission is school resource officers.

And it starts with: "I, Corby Hall, am the inventor, the founder, and the sole owner of FoldAR, a uniquely positioned firearms development company that specializes in producing the most compact rifles that have ever been created." ... By way of my patented technology, FoldAR manufactures and sells full capability rifles that remain fully assembled and deployable from a standard sized backpack within seconds.

verification.notes: FoldAR official site identifies Corby Hall as CEO and inventor and documents the patented, backpack-concealable rifle system; Hall also publicly says he owns the company and patent. The available public records reviewed do not independently establish the additional founder and sole-owner wording.

records.text: Corby Hall said FoldAR's interchangeable barrel system could be used after an assassination to replace the fired barrel and prevent the recovered weapon from matching the bullet profile.
records.speaker: Corby Hall

appearances.snippet: In the case of a FoldAR, you could have the folded rifle in a backpack and another barrel system in it. ... And so you get to a shooting position, you take the rifle out, you unfold it, latch it, take your shot, you fold it, pop the pin, take that barrel system off. ... you shoot a bullet out of one system, one barrel system. And then you swap it over to another and your bullet profile doesn't match. ... As long as you get one of those components out of the mix, then you're effectively scot-free.

verification.notes: FoldAR official documentation confirms tool-free barrel-system changes in seconds. NIST explains that a barrel leaves microscopic marks on a fired bullet and that examiners compare a suspect gun test fire to the crime bullet. Replacing the fired barrel can therefore prevent a crime bullet from matching test bullets fired through the replacement barrel. This does not eliminate cartridge-case marks, DNA, fingerprints, or other forensic links, so the broader claim of being scot-free would be overstated but is not part of this statement.
